## Server acc

ounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-in, for example b
ecause a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nto a named account

before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../accounts`
| The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GET .../acc
ounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its tok
en in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: true`), or

both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```bash theme={"theme
\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/tes
t-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \
"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": { \"client

`hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`
{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always\nread as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`
, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account has makes
`PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in\n`detai

ls.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 characters. One
outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are\nunique on th

e server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, an

d
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Uploaded accounts are h
osted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner\n incl
uded. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** T
he body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`)
or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**\
n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when the issue
r rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account lists `ne
edsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60,

refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the perso
n who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\nis not
a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project accounts:

only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an

account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one account, upl

oad its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
\"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bea

rer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the sam
e steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and\n`mcpja
m cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands
ts. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its setting

s in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` remov
es the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That i
s best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while other acco

unts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens`
still works, and is removed 90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none
when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation:

true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it w
rites\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizat
ionServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to\n`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which na

mes the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code reference](https:/

/docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).
